correctness.rationale: The exact coordinate-update projector representation gives a T-fold positive matrix map. Uniform convergence at zero coupling forces all full-simplex optimizers to the uniform law and localizes their differences to O(sqrt(delta)). The finite-horizon operator expansion has an irreducible star off-diagonal term h_T; the Perron largest eigenvalue is strictly convex on the zero-sum probability tangent space, proving unique global leading-order optimal coefficients and the minimum retention. The geometric average ratio is strictly below one for T>=2. Exact rational matrix recurrences and numerical small-coupling checks from the packaged verifier passed, but are not used to certify the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The same sampling probabilities are usually reused across an optimization run, but a per-step optimum need not optimize a finite stopping horizon. This all-m and all-fixed-T theorem gives the exact leading globally minimax sampling allocation and retention, plus a strict monotone horizon effect with an interpretable geometric-average coefficient. It is structurally motivated by noncommuting coordinate projections, not an arbitrary finite example. Practical benefit vanishes with coupling and no speedup claim is made.
